claude.sample_unit: synthetic physician responses (100 per case version, 10 cases, 2 versions)

links.outcome: LLM bias under paired case variations (framing etc.), with and without forewarning
links.effect: Forewarning reduced cognitive biases by only 6.9% on average; no bias present in controls was eliminated; Occam's razor fallacy increased (77% v. 89%, P = 0.024).
links.quote: No bias present in the control group was eliminated after a forewarning ( Appendix §4, §5 ).

links.outcome: Whether LLM responses appropriately reflect reasoning pitfalls despite seemingly thoughtful, deliberate output
links.effect: Forewarned responses were 50% longer and discussed bias 44.3% v 0.4%, but identified the correct bias in only 5% of responses; irrelevant anchoring bias cited in 16%.
links.quote: A bias forewarning, however, identified the correct bias in only 5% of responses ( Appendix §3 ).

links.outcome: Biased or flawed LLM recommendations that clinicians would need to verify
links.effect: Forewarning decreased overall bias by only 6.9%, and no bias was extinguished completely, highlighting need for clinician vigilance.
links.quote: These findings highlight the need for clinician vigilance when interpreting generated responses that might appear seemingly thoughtful and deliberate.

unlisted_practices: Prompt-based forewarning of cognitive biases to mitigate LLM bias

unlisted_practices: Adding an explicit cognitive-bias forewarning to clinical prompts: “Please keep in mind cognitive biases and other pitfalls of reasoning.”
